What this index is, and is not

Every vendor publishes today's price on its own pricing page. What none of them publish is the trend: what a model cost last quarter, or how a price change lands against everyone else's. This page starts as a single dated snapshot, checked live against each vendor's own page rather than aggregated from a roundup, with the intent to re-check it on a regular cadence and let the history accrue on this same URL.

It is not a benchmark of model quality, and it is not a claim about which model is cheapest for a given task; a model's real cost depends on how many tokens it needs to finish the work, not only its per-token rate (see the FAQ below). It is a dated, sourced record of what each vendor's own page says right now.

Frequently asked questions
How current is this price index?

Every price on this page was re-checked against the vendor's own live pricing page on 2026-09-26. The first edition was checked on 2026-07-23, and each row's note says whether the price changed since then. AI model prices change without much notice, so treat this as a dated snapshot, not a live feed. Click the source link next to any row to see the vendor's current number.
Why is Sakana Fugu not on this list?

This index only covers models priced on the Anthropic, OpenAI and Google pricing pages. When the first edition was checked on 2026-07-23, Sakana had confirmed a billing model (subscription plus usage-based billing with per-request cost reporting) but not an input/output rate card, so it was left out. It was not re-checked for this edition. See our separate breakdown of how Fugu billing works for what is and is not confirmed.
Why do input and output prices differ so much for the same model?

Generating a token (output) takes meaningfully more compute than reading one (input), so every vendor on this page prices output higher, typically 5x to 6x the input rate. The ratio is fairly consistent within a vendor's own model family; it is the absolute price level that varies by vendor and by model tier.
Is a cheaper per-token price always a cheaper task?

No. A more expensive model can still finish a task for less money if it uses meaningfully fewer tokens to reach a correct answer, and a cheaper model can cost more in practice if it needs several retries or a longer reasoning trace. Per-token price is one input to a real cost comparison, not the whole answer; our AI vs Human Employee Cost calculator models the actual task-level tradeoff.
Will this page track price changes over time?

Yes. This is the second edition. Every row carries a note comparing today's price with the first edition of 2026-07-23: in two months OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, Google cut Gemini 3.6 Flash until the end of 2026, and Anthropic kept Claude Sonnet 5 at its launch price. Six models are new since the first edition.
